# Security and Recovery Requirements Checklist: Execution Backend Contracts

**Purpose**: Reviewer gate for fail-closed trust boundaries, credential/privacy exclusions, stale
evidence, cancellation, checkpoint compatibility, fencing, reconciliation, and migration requirements
**Created**: 2026-09-01
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an
item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Trust Boundary Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are adapter commands, observations, profile evidence, reports, routing inputs, checkpoints, and usage all classified as untrusted until Moonshift validation/derivation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §FR-016–FR-017, §FR-029]
- [x] CHK002 Are credentials, tokens, cookies, consumer sessions, raw provider errors, private reasoning, raw transcripts, arbitrary paths, and unclassified extensions prohibited at every durable/public destination? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-016–FR-017]
- [x] CHK003 Are payload size, depth, count, sequence, decimal, timestamp, identifier, and extension namespace boundaries documented for every contract family? [Completeness, Plan §Security, Contracts README §Contract rules]
- [x] CHK004 Are authority lease, fencing token, connection configuration revision, adapter release, profile, and freshness bindings required for probe, conformance, route, start, cancel, and resume? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010–FR-011, §FR-019–FR-023]
- [x] CHK005 Are context classification, minimized manifest, allowed destination, policy, capability, budget, and deadline requirements preserved across initial start and resume? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, §FR-018, §FR-022–FR-023]
- [x] CHK006 Are audit requirements complete for accepted, rejected, stale, duplicate, cancelled, blocked, reconciled, and support-status-changing paths? [Completeness, Spec §FR-032, US1–US4]

## Fail-Closed Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is the precedence among malformed evidence, unknown versions/capabilities, expired evidence, health degradation, unavailable auth, and conformance failure explicitly defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005–FR-008, US1-AS3]
- [x] CHK008 Is every silent-downgrade dimension named and tied to a blocked/queued outcome rather than a best-effort fallback? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018–FR-020, SC-005]
- [x] CHK009 Is stale-result handling explicit about preserving historical evidence while preventing it from refreshing current qualification? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, Data Model §ProbeSnapshot]
- [x] CHK010 Is route revalidation defined as creating/requiring a successor decision rather than mutating or informally refreshing a committed route? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, US3-AS5]
- [x] CHK011 Are cancellation acknowledgment, confirmed termination, unknown remote work, effect uncertainty, and reconciliation-required states clearly distinct? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013–FR-014, US2-AS3]
- [x] CHK012 Is checkpoint incompatibility defined across contract/profile, capability, classification, context, artifact, budget, event position, model, and effect requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022–FR-024, US3-AS4]

## Recovery and Effect Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Do resume requirements consistently require old-authority fencing and effect reconciliation before successor execution authority is issued? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023, US3-AS3]
- [x] CHK014 Does exactly-one accepted terminal result remain consistent with cancellation and reconciliation lifecycles that may continue after backend termination? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012–FR-014]
- [x] CHK015 Do deduplication requirements distinguish harmless identical replay from conflicting duplicate evidence requiring failure/reconciliation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK016 Do checkpoint/session requirements consistently keep provider or harness session hints optional and non-authoritative? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022–FR-023, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK017 Do usage and budget requirements preserve remaining authority across checkpoint/resume without aggregating incompatible units or inventing conversions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-022, Research R-006]
- [x] CHK018 Do Feature 001 external-effect, recovery, supervisor-control, and evidence guarantees remain explicit non-regression requirements throughout migration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-034, SC-010]

## Exception and Attack Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are contradictory capability claims, forged support status, tampered report, changed configuration, late probe, and stale health covered as trust-boundary attacks? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005, §FR-029]
- [x] CHK020 Are event gaps, sequence overflow, conflicting duplicates, post-terminal output, multiple results, oversized values, and decimal overflow covered? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-010–FR-017]
- [x] CHK021 Are provider-field, credential-shaped, prompt-injection-shaped, private-reasoning-shaped, path traversal, and extension-namespace abuse requirements addressed? [Coverage, Spec US2-AS4, §FR-016–FR-017]
- [x] CHK022 Are auth expiry, conformance expiry, health change, capacity loss, budget exhaustion, and policy change between route and start covered? [Coverage, Spec US3-AS5, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK023 Are corrupt hash, missing artifact, incompatible version, insufficient classification, pending unknown effect, and lost session-hint checkpoint cases covered? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-022–FR-024]
- [x] CHK024 Are crash boundaries defined before/during/after probe, qualification, report, support derivation, route commit, start, cancel, result, usage, checkpoint, and resume? [Coverage, Plan §Test Strategy]

## Migration, Backup, and Reversibility

- [x] CHK025 Are migration requirements explicit about additive tables, immutable legacy evidence, legacy `1.0` read mapping, and new-write version behavior? [Completeness, Plan §Data, Research R-008]
- [x] CHK026 Are backup/restore requirements complete for catalog, probe/health, qualification, report/hash/artifact, route, usage, and legacy records as one consistent set? [Completeness, Plan §Data, Quickstart §Full gate]
- [x] CHK027 Is partial restore behavior defined to fail closed rather than deriving qualification or support from incomplete evidence? [Recovery, Plan §Data, Gap]
- [x] CHK028 Is rollback bounded to application/checkpoint and pre-migration backup semantics without implying destructive reverse migration? [Clarity, Plan §Data]

## Acceptance and Scope Quality

- [x] CHK029 Can zero-leakage, zero-downgrade, checkpoint block/resume, and no-duplicate-effect outcomes be objectively measured from named fixture populations? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, §SC-005–SC-006]
- [x] CHK030 Are no-network, no-credential, no-real-support, no-arbitrary-shell, and no-production-deployment constraints stated as executable acceptance boundaries rather than prose assumptions? [Scope, Spec §FR-033–FR-035, SC-010]
- [x] CHK031 Are open decisions OD-005–OD-010 prevented from being silently resolved by this feature's fixture configuration or documentation? [Governance, Spec §Assumptions, §Exclusions]
- [x] CHK032 Are security and recovery requirements traceable to the exact contracts, data entities, tests, and evidence expected in the later task decomposition? [Traceability, Plan §Test Strategy]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and
  `$speckit-clarify`.
